business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Caliber is a mining operator that manages overburden removal, coal extraction and coal logistics together as an integrated services provider, offering end-to-end services including coal extraction, overburden removal, coal loading/unloading, road transportation and rail coordination. It provides contractual coal extraction and overburden removal at open cast mines it does not own, primarily for Coal India subsidiaries WCL and NCL, and runs a logistics business for coal and iron ore. Operations are located in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Western Coalfields Limited (WCL) — Largest mining customer (Coal India subsidiary): Marquee and largest mining customer across FY24-FY26
- Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) — Largest mining customer (Coal India subsidiary): Marquee and largest mining customer across FY24-FY26
- KSR Freight Carriers — Key logistics customer and related party: Partnership firm; promoter Anuj Krishanlal Chadda is a partner
- KKC Group — Former customer (Baranj mine) and related party: Baranj contract completed February 7, 2025
- Shree Chadda Roadlines — Partnership firm associated with promoter Anuj Krishanlal Chadda

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Integrated end-to-end coal mining and logistics services provider offering coal extraction, overburden removal, coal loading and unloading, road transportation and coordination of rail transportation as a one-stop provider. Owns its fleet (1,811 owned and 100 leased vehicles, plant and machinery as of April 30, 2026), enabling cost, scheduling and customer-service advantages over leased fleets. Conducts in-house and preventive maintenance at its own workshops (headquarters at Chandrapur plus seven mining sites), providing cost savings. Procures high-speed diesel a month in advance directly from local refineries at favourable rates to reduce diesel expenses and short-term price exposure. Maximises economies of scale through integration of mining and logistics services, and uses ERP across operations, procurement, dispatch and accounting.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue mix shifting toward coal mining services (69.44% of revenue in FY24 to 86.08% in FY26) and away from logistics (27.87% to 12.44%)
- Operating EBITDA margin steady at around 25% (25.51% FY24, 24.45% FY25, 25.69% FY26)
- Working capital cycle of 37 days in FY26 (47 days FY25, 32 days FY24); receivable days improving from 52 (FY24) to 42 (FY26)
- Net Debt/Equity improving from 2.44x in FY24 to 1.62x in FY26 amid heavy capex in fleet
- Order book growth from Rs 5,66,829.69 lakhs (March 31, 2026) to Rs 9,55,089.08 lakhs (May 15, 2026)

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue steady growth of the operating business through the promoters' strategic vision and industry experience
- Invest in vehicles, plant and machinery to increase overburden removal and mining capacity
- Maintain in-house maintenance for cost savings and operating efficiencies

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Caliber has been expanding capacity through large investment in vehicles, plant and machinery, increasing overburden removal by 88.18% from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026. As of April 30, 2026 it owned 1,811 and leased 100 vehicles, plant and machinery (including 883 mining tippers, 362 tip trailers, 162 excavators, 64 loaders, 65 bulldozers and 32 graders). Net proceeds of the Offer are proposed to fund further capital expenditure for the purchase of commercial vehicles, plant and machinery.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated one-stop provider covering coal extraction, overburden removal, loading/unloading, road transportation and rail coordination
- Large owned fleet of 1,811 owned (plus 100 leased) vehicles, plant and machinery as of April 30, 2026
- In-house maintenance workshops at headquarters and seven mining sites providing cost savings and efficiencies
- Marquee customers being Coal India subsidiaries WCL and NCL
- Large order book of Rs 9,55,089.08 lakhs (including advance work orders) as of May 15, 2026
- Revenue from operations grew at a CAGR of 32.67% from FY24 to FY26

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration on Coal India subsidiaries WCL and NCL — Largest mining customers are WCL and NCL; loss or reduced awards from a few customers could materially affect revenue
- Does not own the mines or coal reserves — Operates purely on contractual mining services; termination or penalties under mining contracts could adversely affect operations
- Contract termination / suspension risk — Parsa mine operations suspended since September 1, 2023 and continuing; mining contracts may be terminated or penalties demanded on certain events
- Mining operations subject to operating risks — Accidents, flooding, machinery/equipment failures and unavailability of diesel fuel and water could decrease production or increase cost of production
- Health and safety regulatory exposure — Violation of health and safety laws could lead to temporary shutdown of mines/processing facilities and costly compliance measures
- Capital intensity and leverage — Heavy investment in vehicles, plant and machinery; Net Debt/Equity of 1.62x and Net Debt/Operating EBITDA of 2.44x in FY26
- Related party transactions — Ongoing related party transactions (e.g., KSR Freight Carriers, KKC Group) that may continue in the future

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Fund capital expenditure for the purchase of commercial vehicles, plant and machinery from the Net Proceeds of the Offer.**
- **Repay or prepay, in full or part, certain borrowings availed by the Company using the Net Proceeds.**
- **Execute the order book of Rs 9,55,089.08 lakhs (including advance work orders) as of May 15, 2026, over an anticipated 32-68 months for mining/overburden and 12-60 months for logistics contracts.**
- **Continue expanding overburden removal and mining capacity through investment in vehicles, plant and machinery (having grown overburden removal 88.18% from FY24 to FY26).**
- **Continue steady growth of the operating business leveraging promoters' strategic vision and understanding of the mining and logistics business.**
- **Maintain in-house maintenance and preventive maintenance of vehicles, plant and machinery at headquarters and seven mining sites for cost savings and efficiencies.**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
